schema_note: M0-T03 probe record. Every field below was observed, not assumed. Anything not observed is null with a reason.

hermes.install_source: git clone at the pinned commit, then an editable install (uv pip install -e .)
hermes.install_note: Owner approved the git install. A git+https wheel build is REFUSED BY UPSTREAM: setup.py raises RuntimeError('Building wheels or sdists for hermes-agent is not supported. Hermes is distributed via the shell installer, Docker image, or Nix.'). The supported paths are the shell installer, Docker, Nix, or an editable install from a clone. The editable install at the pinned commit succeeded and the API surface below was read from 0.21.3 itself. For the M3 runtime, Docker is the right choice: it matches upstream's supported distribution and the isolation plan section 4.2 already requires.

hermes.custom_tool_injection_finding: Confirmed on 0.21.3, not only 0.19.0. AIAgent.__init__ exposes none of mcp_servers, tools, extra_tools, custom_tools or tool_registry, and toolsets.create_custom_toolset(name, description, tools, includes) composes existing tool NAMES only. EpisAlpha's typed tools therefore reach Hermes over MCP, configured by file (mcp.json under $HERMES_HOME/~/.hermes). MCP tools surface with an 'mcp_' name prefix, which create_custom_toolset can then allowlist: EpisAlpha MCP server -> mcp.json -> create_custom_toolset('episalpha', tools=['mcp_...']) -> enabled_toolsets=['episalpha']. This is the M3-T01/M3-T03 design, still to be proven with a working probe before the runtime is built on it. PROVEN by M3-T01 on 2026-10-10: see hermes.mcp_path_proof.
hermes.end_to_end_agent_run_reason: Not attempted. M0-T03 stops before building a runtime, and driving a real agent turn with EpisAlpha tools depends on the MCP adapter decision above.

mcp_path_proof.hermes_install: git clone at c1488ac947c9bc33fd65ec464548dc9d8edd6122 (0.21.3) in .episalpha/vendor/hermes-agent, editable install with the [mcp] extra (mcp 2.0.0) in its own venv .episalpha/vendor/hermes-venv
mcp_path_proof.server: scripts/probe_mcp.py: stdlib newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio, legacy initialize handshake
mcp_path_proof.tool_name_prefix: mcp__<server>__<tool>, e.g. mcp__episalpha__echo_span (double underscores; the M0-T03 note 'mcp_' was wrong)
mcp_path_proof.tool_search_finding: With tools.tool_search.enabled at its default 'auto', Hermes replaced the MCP tool with tool_search/tool_describe/tool_call meta-tools; the model spent 3 requests discovering the tool and never called it. With tools.tool_search.enabled: 'off' in config.yaml the model saw exactly ['mcp__episalpha__echo_span'], called it once and answered with the exact quote in 2 API calls. EpisAlpha's harness must set tool_search off.
mcp_path_proof.live_requests_spent: about 6 (first attempt 3 plus a summary request, second attempt 2)

observation_notes.response_format_json_schema_honored: One call: the content parsed as JSON matching the requested keys. response_format is NOT in the :free supported_parameters listing, so this may be the model following the prompt rather than the provider enforcing the schema. The relay stays tool_choice-only (A3) either way.
observation_notes.no_fallbacks_accepted: provider.allow_fallbacks=false was sent with the forced tool call and accepted (HTTP 200).
observation_notes.reasoning_tokens: One forced tool call: completion_tokens 213, of which reasoning_tokens 122; prompt_tokens 411. Reasoning is reported inside completion_tokens. Whether max_tokens caps reasoning was not probed directly.
observation_notes.tool_choice_required_honored: M3-T03, 2026-10-11: one call with tool_choice 'required' returned finish_reason 'stop' and a pseudo tool call written into the content text. Named tool_choice (M0-T04) works; the relay forces the named submit tool on each stage's last request instead.

model_route.pricing_note: usage.cost was present and 0 (free tier, OpenRouter credits, not EUR). cost_eur stays None in v0.1 (global constitution article 13).

model_route_history.pricing_note: No pricing field observed in the usage payload, so cost stays unknown (plan section 3.8, acceptance row A22).

consequences_for_episalpha: Structured final output must come from forced tool-call arguments, never from response_format. The OpenAI-compatible surface accepts response_format and silently ignores it, returning prose - a silent failure, not an error.
The bounded output repair in plan section 3.6 step 7 has a concrete justification: the host must validate and repair candidate JSON itself.
glm-5.3 is a reasoning model: trivial answers cost 600-1600 completion tokens. The 4000-token per-call cap in plan section 3.8 is workable but tight, and should be measured again at M3-T02.
Hermes exact-pins its dependencies, so it must live in its own environment or container and never share the application virtualenv (plan section 4.2).
